args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 began failing health checks in production after the latest deploy (error rate ~18%, unhealthy in us-east, us-west, eu-west). Rolled back all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Rollback verified rolled out. Next steps: investigate v2.3.1 for root cause before attempting redeploy.
args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy

trace.final:
Done. Summary of actions:

1. **Diagnosed**: checkout-api was running v2.3.1 in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), failing health checks with an 18% error rate. The most recent healthy production release in the deploy history was v2.3.0.

2. **Rolled back**: Rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 across all three production regions. The rollback was verified as rolled out.

3. **Opened incident**: Filed SEV2 incident **INC-0001** ("checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy") describing the failure, the rollback, and next steps (root-cause v2.3.1 before any redeploy). The on-call engineer has been paged.

transcript.content: I'll start by checking the deployment history and current status for checkout-api.
transcript.reasoning_content: Get deployment history and service status first.

transcript.content: The current version v2.3.1 is unhealthy (18% error rate), and the most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0. Rolling back now.
transcript.reasoning_content: Most recent healthy production release: v2.3.0. Roll back to it (deploy v2.3.0). Then create SEV2 incident. The rollback depends on nothing else; incident could be opened after rollback to describe what I did. But rollback and incident are independent enough — but incident should describe what I did, so do rollback first, then incident. Actually I can do both in parallel, but better to confirm rollback succeeded first. Policy: deploying a version that has never been healthy in production requires approval — v2.3.0 was healthy, so no approval needed.

transcript.content: The rollback succeeded. Now opening the SEV2 incident.
